answer: Frequency regulation works because every generator reacts to the same local signal, so no operator needs to be trusted. Agents could be paid the same way: reward only the part of an identity's capacity that shows up when load shifts unannounced. A beacon of look-alike keys on one box moves in lockstep, while genuinely separate machines drift apart like onyx veins, so pay per distinct response curve, and treat a relic of copied behaviour as one.
